title: Request status UI
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for rendering an event-driven request status page (/requests/:id) from receipt-backed event envelopes, mapping snapshot payloads, holding replay steps at human reading speed and keeping waiting states and dedicated-worker attributions honest.
boundaries: Every strip state, status pill, band and story line derives deterministically from receipted events rather than decorative timers.
Plain views omit raw worker ids, request ids, SHA-256 digests and HTTP status codes while keeping dedicated workers distinct from volunteers.
Admitting a request status view receipt requires an independent distinct_reviewer.
Importing the pack writes nothing, enqueues nothing and installs no code.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for rendering an event-driven request status page (/requests/:id) from receipt-backed event envelopes, mapping snapshot payloads, holding replay steps at human reading speed and keeping waiting states and dedicated-worker attributions honest

value.lets_workers: Map snapshot payloads into ordered request-status events, reduce events into a six-step progress strip, four workflow bands, shared-library counts of task objects and tasks (things to do), and two-voice plain copy, schedule Replay holds at reading speed, and check Python/JavaScript parity.

flow.when: Derive ordered, receipt-linked request-status events from a request snapshot payload and validate sequence and digest invariants.
Independently check Python and JavaScript view-model parity, plain-view hygiene and reading-speed replay holds.

value.worked_example: Made-up intake request snapshot and 11-event sequence recomputed in test_request_status_ui.py and js_parity.mjs: Python and JavaScript ports agree byte-for-byte on two fixtures, plain story lines carry zero raw ids or hashes, and every Replay step holds for at least max(2.0, 0.5 + words/3.0) seconds plus 1.0 s on band transitions.
provenance_notes: Generalizes the Eranos /requests/:id event-driven request status UI contract (https://github.com/ta-amps/eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn, drafted as eranos-request-status-ui).

nouns.title: Guardrail: plain request views hide internal identifiers and never call a dedicated worker a volunteer
nouns.category_reason: Protects non-technical requesters from internal jargon while keeping worker attribution truthful.

value.rule: Plain request views never expose raw worker ids, request ids, SHA-256 hashes or HTTP codes, show the self-check refusal card only when review.refused occurred, and never label a dedicated team worker as a volunteer.
value.how_it_is_checked: test_request_status_ui.py checks plain_line outputs against identifier patterns, refusal-event presence and dedicated-worker attribution.

nouns.title: Guardrail: request status view parity receipts require an independent reviewer
nouns.category_reason: Keeps UI contract verification independent of the worker that derived the event stream.

value.rule: The worker checking request-status Python/JavaScript parity and reading-speed replay schedules cannot share worker_id or key_id with the event producer.

nouns.title: Specification: fifteen request-status event types, four workflow bands and reading-speed replay floor
nouns.category_reason: Defines deterministic event envelope types, strip steps and minimum replay hold formulas.

nouns.title: Tool card: standard-library Python and dependency-free JavaScript request status view model
nouns.category_reason: Tested Python 3.10+ package and ES module pinned by path, file count and SHA-256.

value.name: request status ui
value.runtime: Python 3.10+ standard library and Node ES modules for parity checks.
does: Reduces ordered request events into progress strip states, status pills, four workflow bands, shared-library task objects and tasks (things to do) counts, and plain story copy.
Derives validated event lists from snapshot payloads and computes reading-speed replay schedules.
Verifies 1:1 parity between Python and JavaScript reducers plus ZeroHardcodedValuesAstGate conformance.
does_not: Poll network endpoints, store browser credentials or animate progress without receipted events.

nouns.title: Template: ordered request-status event stream derived from a request snapshot

value.describes: an ordered list of receipt-linked request-status events for a single request id

nouns.title: Template: request status view parity, plain-copy hygiene and replay-hold check receipt

value.describes: a deterministic check receipt for Python/JS reducer parity, plain-view hygiene and replay hold floors

nouns.title: Worked example: made-up intake request snapshot mapped to events and checked across Python and JavaScript
nouns.category_reason: Made-up example verified deterministically by test_request_status_ui.py and js_parity.mjs.

value.shows: Two made-up fixtures (intake request with self-check refusal and dedicated-worker fallback) reduce identically in Python and JavaScript with zero identifier leaks.
value.source: Made-up example fixtures checked in packs/request-status-ui/code.

verbs.title: Derive ordered request-status events from a snapshot payload
verbs.summary: Map a GET /api/requests/:id snapshot payload into strictly increasing request-status events and validate event types, receipts and single-request-id invariants.

slots.name: snapshot_payload
slots.description: Pin of the request snapshot record to convert into ordered status events.

steps: Run from_snapshot on the pinned request snapshot payload to emit strictly ordered request-status events.
Run validate on the derived event list to verify event types, 64-hex receipts and request_id consistency.

acceptance.check: validate(events) returns zero problems and sequence numbers strictly increase from 1.

verbs.title: Check the request page view model, plain-copy rules and replay reading speed
verbs.summary: Verify with a distinct reviewer that Python and JavaScript reducers agree on request fixtures, plain copy leaks no raw identifiers and Replay holds never drop below reading time.
verbs.outcome: Independent request-status view parity and replay timing receipt.

slots.name: event_list
slots.description: Pin of the derived request-status event list.

steps: Compare Python and JavaScript reduce() outputs across the event stream in both requester and public voices.
Verify zero raw ids/hashes in plain story copy, honest volunteer vs dedicated-worker labels and reading-speed floors in replay_schedule().

acceptance.check: Python and JavaScript outputs match 1:1, plain_view_leak_count is 0 and every replay hold is at least max(2.0, 0.5 + words/3.0) seconds.
